tool_input.description: Probe FastDateParser behaviors to validate test assumptions

result:
Not a git repo, so no diff check needed — the only file I created/modified is the new test class itself.

## Summary

I created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/FastDateParserAgentTest.java` (JUnit 5, matching the project's existing test style), with 27 self-contained tests covering happy-path parsing, locale-sensitive text/timezone strategies, ISO-8601 and week-year patterns, getters, `equals`/`hashCode`/`toString`, serialization, two-digit-year century adjustment, and boundary/error cases (invalid input, out-of-range `ParsePosition`, overflowing digit runs, unsupported pattern letters, unterminated quotes, null pattern/time zone).

All 27 tests pass. I did not find any bugs in `FastDateParser` — every behavior I probed first against the real class (error-index semantics, graceful handling of digit-overflow instead of a leaked `NumberFormatException`, century-boundary year adjustment, GMT/ISO-8601 offset parsing, week-date resolution, defensive `TimeZone` copies, and null/invalid-argument rejection) matched the documented contract, so no test is left failing.
